evidence.reason: The lstat guard at line 279 exists to refuse non-regular paths (lines 290-291 refuse any untracked symlink, and tracked symlinks are read with readlink), so the leaf's validated inode is the thing the function intends to snapshot. Line 304 then re-resolves the path with readFile, which follows symlinks; if the leaf is swapped for a symlink after the check, the blob stored at line 311 contains bytes from outside the repository, defeating the existing refusal rather than adding a new requirement. This is an implementation slip in intended behavior, not a proposal to enlarge scope: no new check, lock, or approval is introduced, and the fix is the ordinary one of reading through the handle that was validated (O_NOFOLLOW plus dev/ino comparison) rather than re-resolving the path. The finding correctly scopes the exposure (writer access during capture, outgoing scanner still gating submission) and notes the POSIX-only constant, so a platform fallback can be handled by the same small repair without an owner decision.
